title: Admissible Forgetting as a Scientific Operation: What May a Model Omit Without Losing the Consequence of Interest?
summary: This paper candidate develops “Admissible Forgetting as a Scientific Operation: What May a Model Omit Without Losing the Consequence of Interest?” from material already present in the Lab corpus. Its current claim ceiling is philosophical synthesis and translation of reduction/model abstraction questions; must not duplicate Information Mechanics novelty claims. The current artifact state is materialized methodological section; philosophy projection. The next evidence obligation is paired examples/nonexamples where an omission is harmless versus consequence-destroying. Prior to promotion, it requires review against idealization, abstraction, coarse-graining, model reduction, sufficient statistics, invariance, causal abstraction and philosophy of modeling.

title: AI as Forge: Alternating Breadth and Depth in Machine-Assisted Scientific Inquiry
summary: This paper candidate takes as its central research question: “Does alternating breadth-first comparison with depth-first reduction improve the auditability, reconstruction quality, and defect discovery of machine-assisted research relative to breadth-only, depth-only, and unconstrained agent workflows?” Its current claim ceiling is research-workflow proposal and testable method; no superiority claim before comparison experiments. The current artifact state is materialized methodological note with explicit algorithm and guardrails. The next evidence obligation is compare alternating breadth/depth against breadth-only, depth-only, and unconstrained agent/research baselines. Prior to promotion, it requires review against human-AI scientific discovery, literature-based discovery, search strategies, abduction, iterative deepening, research agents, scientific workflows and sensemaking.

title: Failure as Evidence: Counterexamples, Failed Reductions, and Negative Results as First-Class Scientific State
summary: This paper candidate develops “Failure as Evidence: Counterexamples, Failed Reductions, and Negative Results as First-Class Scientific State” from material already present in the Lab corpus. Its current claim ceiling is methodological argument for preserving structured failures; not a new theory of falsification. The current artifact state is explicit methodological principle; mined philosophy paper. The next evidence obligation is compare research records that preserve versus discard failed paths on later audit/reuse tasks. Prior to promotion, it requires review against popperian falsification, severe testing, negative results, null results, adversarial science, counterexample-guided refinement and open science.

title: The Represented State Space Is Not the Observed State Space: Correspondence as a Scientific Testing Problem
summary: This paper candidate takes as its central research question: “What distinct scientific errors arise when the state space admitted by a model does not correspond to the states and transitions observable in the target system?” Its current claim ceiling is philosophy of modeling and measurement synthesis with a proposed defect taxonomy. The current artifact state is substantial methodological source; distinct paper thesis. The next evidence obligation is worked examples where missing, collapsed, permitted, or forbidden states produce different scientific defects. Prior to promotion, it requires review against measurement theory, model-based science, data-model distinction, constructive empiricism, inverse problems, model discrepancy and observational equivalence.

title: Where Did the Scientific Error Enter? A Representation-Level Taxonomy of Boundary, Measurement, Model, and Test Defects
summary: This paper candidate develops “Where Did the Scientific Error Enter?
